edits.html:
Confirming High Blood Pressure in an Adolescent

High automated reading at a sports physical · confirm by auscultation, then stage

Source vignette Pt — 17 yo M at a pre-participation examination for football; feels well; no illnesses, medications or family history; BMI 29; automated oscillometric reading 138/88 mm Hg, stated as the 95th percentile for age and height, then 140/89 mm Hg on the same device; rest of the examination normal · Q — the most appropriate next step in diagnosis; options spanned auscultatory measurement, echocardiography, 24-hour ambulatory monitoring and repeat device readings daily for 3 days or in 2 weeks
The decision point

Automated oscillometric devices tend to read higher than auscultation for both systolic and diastolic pressure. A high device reading needs confirmation by auscultation, even after the same device has repeated it. Take at least two auscultatory readings at that visit and average them. The averaged auscultatory value sets the category and the recheck interval.

From age 13, the 2017 AAP (American Academy of Pediatrics) guideline uses fixed cutoffs that match the adult categories. By those cutoffs, 138/88 mm Hg falls in stage 1 and 140/89 mm Hg in stage 2. Device readings are not staged until auscultation confirms them. Ambulatory monitoring, echocardiography and drug therapy all come after that confirmation.

Defining criteria, age 13 and older Confirming a high reading — repeat by auscultation at the same visit and average the readings; a device reading alone is not staged · Elevated blood pressure — systolic 120 to 129 mm Hg with diastolic below 80 mm Hg · Stage 1 hypertension — 130/80 to 139/89 mm Hg · Stage 2 hypertension — 140/90 mm Hg or higher · Hypertension diagnosis — auscultatory-confirmed readings of 130/80 mm Hg or higher at 3 separate visits
Management ladder — high blood pressure in an adolescent
TierInterventionEscalate when
1Screening reading at a routine visit; an oscillometric device is acceptable. Yearly from age 3, and at every visit with obesity, kidney disease, diabetes, prior coarctation or a drug that raises blood pressureReading of 120/80 mm Hg or higher
2Repeat by auscultation at the same visit, at least 2 readings, and average themAveraged auscultatory value in the elevated or hypertensive range; that value sets the stage
3Recheck by auscultation on a schedule set by stage: elevated, lifestyle advice and recheck in 6 months; stage 1, lifestyle advice and recheck in 1 to 2 weeks; stage 2, lifestyle advice and specialty referral within 1 weekElevated readings for 1 year, or stage 1 readings at 3 visits
424-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring to confirm hypertensionHypertension confirmed: evaluate for secondary causes and end-organ damage
5Lifestyle change first: the DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) diet and moderate to vigorous activity 3 to 5 days a week. Echocardiography for left ventricular hypertrophy when drug therapy is consideredLifestyle change fails, especially with left ventricular hypertrophy, symptoms or stage 2 without a modifiable cause: start a drug
Scenario bank
Guideline history The 2004 Fourth Report defined hypertension as a reading at or above the 95th percentile at every age, and older questions still use that definition. The 2017 AAP guideline set fixed adult cutoffs from age 13 and kept percentiles only for children under 13. Under 13, stage 1 starts at the 95th percentile for sex, age and height, or at 130/80 mm Hg if that is lower. From age 13, stage 1 starts at 130/80 mm Hg regardless of percentile.
Exit ramps A symptomatic adolescent, or a reading above 180/120 mm Hg, goes to the emergency department · Stage 1 or stage 2 readings call for a leg blood pressure; an arm reading higher than the leg suggests coarctation of the aorta · Confirmed hypertension opens a search for secondary causes and end-organ damage
Pearls Electrocardiography is not used to look for left ventricular hypertrophy in a hypertensive child; echocardiography is · Lifestyle change aimed at obesity is the first treatment for most adolescent hypertension · How NBME framed it: with the device reading already repeated, the key is a measurement method, not a diagnosis, heart test or later recheck
Pairs with Part I Hypertension: Workup & Drug Choice covers confirmation, baseline tests and drug choice in adults. Part I Secondary Hypertension covers the causes to test for once hypertension is confirmed.
Transferable rule A high blood pressure from an automated device is confirmed by averaged auscultatory readings before it is staged, monitored, imaged or treated.
Sequencing trapEchocardiography looks for left ventricular hypertrophy once drug therapy is considered, and this reading is not yet confirmed.
Sequencing trapAmbulatory monitoring is accurate, but it follows auscultatory office readings that stay elevated for 1 year or in stage 1 across 3 visits.
Unchecked attributeDaily device readings for 3 days repeat the same overestimate; the method must change, not the number of readings.
True-fact-wrong-slotA 1 to 2 week recheck follows stage 1 confirmed by auscultation, but a repeat device reading in 2 weeks confirms nothing.
